study: K-quant decode is compute bound in llmx and bandwidth bound in mx
scope: Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 and Q5_K_M, same machine, same session, same two compare_cpu binaries, six threads, eight matched rounds each, identical committed HF token IDs in both arms. The llmx arm includes the fused Q5_K decode dot.
finding: Decode is memory-bandwidth bound, so moving from Q8_0 (about 1.06 bytes per weight) to Q5_K (about 0.69) should make it FASTER. mx does exactly that: 41.44 -> 58.30 tok/s, +41%. llmx goes the other way: 40.93 -> 15.98, -61%. A smaller quant making llmx slower means the llmx K-quant decode path is limited by per-weight unpacking and float conversion, not by memory traffic. Q8_0 decode sits at parity (0.99x) because its fused dequant+FMA matvec is cheap enough to stay bandwidth bound.
consequence: Prefill work cannot close this. Both quants are already above the floor in prefill (1.50x and 1.41x here). The gap is entirely in K-quant decode.
next: Test whether quantizing the activation vector to 8 bits and taking an integer dot product recovers the bandwidth-bound behaviour, as mx does. That is a larger change than a fused dot and affects every quant type, so it needs its own prospective plan and its own HF gate.
limits: One model family, one size, one thread count. Bytes per weight is computed from block layouts, not measured DRAM traffic; no bandwidth counter was read. The compute-bound conclusion follows from the direction of the change across quants, not from a hardware counter.
